title: Complete requirements map, strategy view, roadmap; cite by heading
summary: Redo the failed retry: deliver the full BRIEF.md requirements map plus a strategy view and a roadmap, not a sample table. Files this change edits (CHANGELOG.md, the map, new docs) are cited by heading or quote, never by line number; untouched files such as BRIEF.md may keep file:line cites.

defaults_applied.how: Every row cites a source; cites into edited files use headings or quotes so they cannot drift.
Docs are written for an outside reader.
Verifier checks that cites match the tree.

assumptions: The tree holds only the earlier sample table; the failed attempt's changes were discarded.
Strategy view and roadmap go in separate docs under docs/design/, linked from the map.
Citing BRIEF.md by line is fine because this change does not edit it.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/requirements-map.md covers every requirement in BRIEF.md as rows with IDs, each marked covered, partial, or not covered, replacing the sample table.
No file:line or file:range citation points into any file this change edits (CHANGELOG.md, the map, any new or edited doc); those are cited by heading or short quote.
Line cites into untouched files (BRIEF.md, docs/records.md, etc.) match the tree, and the map states which files may be cited by line and why.
A strategy view (requirements grouped by goal with coverage status) and a roadmap (ordered next steps for partial and uncovered rows, linked to row IDs) exist and are linked from the map.
The CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry describes the map, strategy view and roadmap, says rows quote or paraphrase the requirement (matching the map's Wording section), and has no line-number cites.
Run git status and git diff --stat: only Markdown under docs/ and CHANGELOG.md (and possibly README.md) changed. Run cargo fmt --check to confirm nothing else is affected.

out_of_scope: Code, config, or governance file changes
departures: Full map over all of BRIEF.md plus two new docs is larger than the typical job, so cost and time sit above the reference; the line-cite rule makes drift failures less likely.
